title: The owner of the treatment changed-window and active-count reads conflicts between the DP04 story and the service ownership
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12 (TreatmentQuery.changedBetween and TreatmentQuery.countActive, in process); Ownership Map v1 table treatment and the S2 api rows; RWB-P1-E2010-APP section 12.2, which names the same two reads under RWB-P3-E2004-CON
section: Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence, R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11, R4 naming; legacy RWB-E2-010 sections 4 and 12
description: The legacy stage 2 step read the treatments it needed through two in-process calls on the treatment module. In the 19-service target the table treatment and its REST owner are S2 rwb-treatment, so the two reads belong on the S2 base /api/recovery/treatment/v1. RWB-P1-E2010-APP, the primary slice already written for this legacy key, instead names the changed-window read and the active count under the case contract RWB-P3-E2004-CON and calls them on /api/recovery/case/v1. Both cannot be true, and the DP04 build of rwb-source-data is the consumer either way.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12 'Published interfaces used' lists TreatmentQuery on the treatment module; Ownership Map v1 gives table treatment and four REST operations to S2 rwb-treatment; RWB-P1-E2010-APP section 12.2 lists 'the changed-window and active-count reads of the contract' under P3 rwb-case.
proposed: Publish both reads on the owner of the treatment record: GET /treatments and GET /treatments/active-count on /api/recovery/treatment/v1, and have the DP04 build of rwb-source-data call them there with a fake; the case base keeps the case and the timers and serves no treatment fact.

title: The two operation shapes, the active-state rule and the reference-data read path are fixed by no source document
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12 and section 13; TSD S2 v2 T3.1 and T6.1; FSD S2 A2.1.3.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and DP-11
section: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12; legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12
description: No source names a consumer-facing operation for the treatments changed in a window, nor for the number of active treatments, nor their parameters, their page shape, their maximum page size or their error codes; the legacy step called a Java interface with (from, to) and with no page at all. No source defines which treatment states the active count includes either: the legacy story uses the words 40 active treatments and a count against TreatmentQuery.countActive() without naming the states. The reference-data read of rwb-case is named nowhere as an operation, although DP-07 requires the labels and their version.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 12 gives two Java signatures and no REST shape; TSD S2 T3.1 gives the treatment fields and the field source but no active-state rule; the FSD S2 field catalogues list the same eight treatment fields with no lifecycle rule for the count.
proposed: Fix the two operations as GET /treatments?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size= and GET /treatments/active-count on the S2 base, with page, size, total and the window in the answer, a maximum page size of 1000 and 400 on an empty window; hold the active states as a parameter row of the parameters contract and read the three lists through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{tableCode} with its version.
